description: Vehicle Details: 2018 LAND ROVER RANGE ROVER SPORT HSE  Few luxury SUVs balance sophistication, athletic character, and genuine all-weather capability quite like the Range Rover Sport. This 2018 Land Rover Range Rover Sport HSE, with 105,175 miles, offers the distinctive design, elevated driving position, refined cabin, and commanding personality that have made the Range Rover name recognizable around the world. For the buyer who wants something more distinctive than the typical luxury SUV, this HSE presents a compelling Premium Pre-Owned opportunity at Infiniti of Boerne.  Power comes from a 3.0-liter supercharged V6 producing 340 horsepower and 332 lb-ft of torque, paired with an 8-speed automatic transmission and four-wheel drive. Around San Antonio, cruising Interstate 10 through the Texas Hill Country, or setting out on a long-distance Texas road trip, the Range Rover Sport feels substantial, composed, and purpose-built.  BRITISH LUXURY WITH A SPORTING CHARACTER  The Range Rover Sport occupies an interesting place in the luxury SUV world. It provides the elevated seating position, versatility, and capability buyers expect from a premium SUV while maintaining a more athletic personality than a traditional full-size luxury utility vehicle.  The HSE trim strengthens that formula with an upscale interior environment centered on premium materials and passenger comfort. Leather seating, heated front seats, driver memory functionality, navigation, and premium cabin appointments create an environment appropriate for commuting, entertaining clients, or covering hundreds of highway miles in a day.  Rather than simply surrounding passengers with luxury features, the Range Rover Sport creates a particular kind of driving experience. For an executive, business owner, frequent traveler, or driver who simply appreciates distinctive automotive design, the Range Rover Sport offers personality that is difficult to duplicate.  340 HORSEPOWER WITH FOUR-WHEEL-DRIVE CAPABILITY  The supercharged V6 is central to this HSE's appeal.  Its 340 horsepower and 332 lb-ft of torque provide the kind of effortless acceleration that suits a premium SUV. The 8-speed automatic transmission helps keep power delivery smooth, whether navigating city traffic or accelerating onto a Texas highway.  Four-wheel drive adds another layer of versatility. The Range Rover name has always carried an expectation of capability, and the Sport combines that engineering heritage with a more road-focused luxury experience. Infiniti of Boerne's objective is not to treat a Premium Pre-Owned vehicle as simply another used vehicle. The objective is to carefully select, inspect, prepare, and present it to a standard appropriate for a luxury dealership.  For this Range Rover Sport, that distinction matters.  A DIFFERENT KIND OF LUXURY VALUE  One of the most compelling aspects of purchasing an established luxury vehicle is the opportunity to experience a level of engineering, craftsmanship, and performance originally positioned much higher in the market while making a substantially different investment than purchasing new.  This 2018 Range Rover Sport HSE illustrates that opportunity particularly well.  The sophisticated styling remains unmistakably Range Rover. Four-wheel drive gives the vehicle year-round versatility, while the premium HSE cabin creates an environment designed for more than basic transportation.  That combination makes this an intriguing option for someone searching for a Premium Pre-Owned Luxury Vehicle near San Antonio or a Pre-Owned Luxury SUV in Texas without wanting the financial commitment associated with a comparable new luxury SUV.  It can also make sense for a buyer who values individuality. DISTINCTIVE LUXURY, THOUGHTFULLY PREPARED  The appeal of this 2018 Land Rover Range Rover Sport HSE isn't based on a single feature.  It is the combination.  The commanding Range Rover design. You look away for just a second and suddenly the vehicle in front of you has stopped. That's when the forward collision mitigation system comes to life. Pedestrians don't always stop, look, and listen, but with Pedestrian Impact Prevention, your vehicle is equipped to better see them and avoid them. You checked the mirror, looked over your shoulder and still nearly collided with the car next to you. An active blind spot system not only alerts you to the presence of a vehicle to your sides or rear but helps prevent you from making an unsafe lane change.  Replace fear and uncertainty with the confidence and safety of the Active blind spot system. Forward collision mitigation - Forward thinking. You look away for just a second and suddenly the vehicle in front of you has stopped. That's when the forward collision mitigation system comes to life.  When it senses an impending impact, it will activate a combination of features to help prevent or reduce the severity of an accident.  Forward collision mitigation is always looking ahead. Pedestrian impact prevention - An extra step toward safety.  Pedestrians don't always stop, look, and listen, but with Pedestrian Impact Prevention, your vehicle is equipped to better see them and avoid them. This system constantly monitors the road ahead to identify and track pedestrians. It projects that image to an interior display screen, AND should an impact become likely, Pedestrian impact prevention takes steps to avoid a collision. Hands-on cruise control. Set it and forget it. Road trips used to be stressful. Cruise control only managed speed, but not distance or safety. Now, with hands-on cruise control, simply set your desired speed and let sensor technology maintain a safe distance between you and surrounding vehicles. It slows you down; speeds you up and even keeps you in your own lane. Meet your ultimate co-pilot with hands-on cruise control.Technology and Telematics Smart device mirroring - Smartphone, meet smart car. You can control your device through your vehicle's infotainment system.  Smart device mirroring brings together safety and convenience by making it easier to find what you're looking for while keeping your eyes on the road. Still the quintessential sports car after four decades, the 2006 Porsche 911 has a unique blend of style, performance and sound that's unmatched by anything on the road. A decade after designing the legendary Volkswagen, Dr. Ferdinand Porsche came up with a sports car derivative of his famous "people's car" called the 356. Light and sporty but notoriously underpowered, the 356 developed a loyal following throughout the 1950s and early '60s. Not wanting to offend their die-hard fans, Porsche executives decided a new model needed to be introduced for 1965 that could carry on the rear-engine tradition made famous by the 356. Ferdinand's son Ferry was commissioned with the task of designing the car, and the result was introduced to the world as the all-new 1965 Porsche 911. Forty years later, the 911 is celebrated around the world as one of the most legendary sports cars ever built, and the Teutonic road warrior has been completely redesigned to commemorate the occasion. Porsche aficionados and the automotive press alike complained when an all-new 911 debuted in 1999 with slippery new styling and a liquid-cooled engine, claiming the car fell a little too far from the 911 family tree. There's no denying that from a performance standpoint, however, this latest generation of the Porsche 911 has been the best ever. Last year, Porsche gave the 911 its first major update since '99. The updated 911 (commonly referred to as the "997") has a cleaner look to it while also containing some retro-themed style elements, such as upright round headlights and flared wheelwells. The interior is now a lot better in terms of comfort and style, and new high-tech options such as satellite navigation and a Bose surround-sound stereo make the German sports car a relatively practical choice for commuters with a need for speed. The standard power plant is a 3.6-liter flat six rated at 325 horsepower and 273 pound-feet of torque, while a new Carrera S model receives a 3.8-liter version of the same engine that produces 355 hp and 295 lb-ft of torque. Apart from the larger displacement, the S differs from the standard Carrera by the following standard equipment: an active suspension system, stability control, larger brakes with red calipers, 19-inch wheels instead of the Carrera's 18-inchers, bi-xenon headlamps, a sportier steering wheel, faux aluminum cabin trim and a silver-colored logo mounted on the rear deck lid. Driven at normal speeds the 911 delivers a firm but mostly pleasant ride that's suitable for daily commutes, but the growl of the flat six behind the driver is a welcome reminder that this is no vanilla passenger car. Lay into the power, and the Porsche 911 comes alive.
